plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: A fragrant evergreen shrub with silvery-gray narrow leaves and dense spikes of small tubular flowers held on slender stems. Widely cultivated in gardens and commercial fields, it attracts bees and butterflies and is prized for its essential oil.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to midsummer (June to August in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Mediterranean region, southern France (Provence), England, and cultivated across temperate North America and Europe
plants.funFact: Lavender was used by the Romans to scent their baths, and its name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'.

plants.name: Rosa canina
plants.description: A vigorous, arching, thorny wild shrub with delicate five-petaled flowers that have a light sweet scent. After flowering it produces bright red rose hips rich in vitamin C. It is common in hedgerows, woodland edges and scrub.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May to July)
plants.location: Europe, northwest Africa, and western Asia; naturalized in North America, Australia and New Zealand
plants.funFact: During World War II, rose hips from the dog rose were collected in Britain to make vitamin C-rich syrup when citrus fruit was scarce.

plants.name: Leucospermum cordifolium
plants.description: A rounded evergreen shrub of the fynbos with striking domed flower heads bristling with long, curved styles that resemble pins in a cushion. The flowers open in vivid shades of orange and red and are a magnet for sunbirds.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere late winter to spring (August to November), with some early blooms in cooler months; often flowering in the winter-wet season in cultivation
plants.location: Western Cape of South Africa; cultivated in Australia, California, and Hawaii
plants.funFact: Pincushion proteas are pollinated by birds, and their seeds are carried by ants into underground nests, which protect them from fire.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: An aquatic perennial whose large, showy flowers rise on tall stalks above round, water-repellent leaves. The blooms open in the morning and close at night, and the plant grows in shallow ponds and wetlands.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early summer to late summer (June to September)
plants.location: Asia from India and China to Japan, southeast Asia and northern Australia; cultivated in ponds worldwide
plants.funFact: Lotus seeds can remain viable for hundreds of years; seeds around 1,300 years old have been successfully germinated.
